_doc: Coding-agent CLIs the Blurt app can hand a recording to, headless. Read by agents.py and by the macOS app (BlurtRecorder: Agents.swift; a copy is bundled into Blurt.app/Contents/Resources). Order of `agents` = default fallback order; the user's order is config record.agents. A custom agent can be added in config record.agent_defs with the same fields. status: how to tell whether it is logged in without spending tokens — `args` run with a 15 s timeout, then: json_key (a bool in the first JSON object of the output) > creds_json ({path, keys}: the file exists and every key is empty → logged out) > logged_out (substrings) > ok_if (substrings, exit 0) > configured_if (regex: has credentials, can't verify them) > env_any / files_any (credentials in env / on disk) > otherwise ('logged_out' | 'unknown'). run: the headless command, {prompt} = the task text — only ever unattended (organising a recording, AI fill-in, routing, drafts) on text taken from the user's screen and voice, so it gets the least privilege that still lets it file items. Its cwd is the session folder (AI fill-in: a scratch folder), never the project; it reads the project's code but writes nothing there. No full-access / yolo modes. claude / gemini: file edits only inside cwd (acceptEdits / auto_edit) and shell commands only the skill scripts an organizing run uses, each pinned to its absolute path ({scripts} = the skill's scripts folder; the prompt names the same path) — no other command, no other script. codex: its workspace-write sandbox, writable = cwd + {writable} (one `--add-dir` each: the inbox store, every project's .blurt store, and a uv cache of its own — env UV_CACHE_DIR, BLURT_NO_INDEX; agents.py sandbox_env); never $BLURT_HOME (config.json, the jobs and their hook settings, index.db) nor the shared uv cache, so nothing it writes runs outside the sandbox later; network stays on because uv resolves the scripts' dependencies. A project's .blurt/config.json can't define agents (agents.py config). kimi / opencode: their own -p / run defaults (flags not verified). Hand-offs the user starts are interactive.session and keep their own modes. verified: 'run' = a real headless run was checked, 'cli' = flags checked with --help only, 'docs' = from the CLI's documentation. WP2 fields (agents.py detect / command / install): version = args printing the version; events = args appended to run for machine-readable progress + its format; headless: false = never run unattended (skip it in the auto chain); interactive = {url (placeholders {repo_q} {prompt_q}, max_prompt), | terminal (args after the bin, run in the user's terminal; paste_prompt: put the prompt on the clipboard), | copy_prompt}; app = {macos: path} for app-only agents; skill_dir = where the blurt skill is linked; mcp = {args (+check: args that exit 0 when already added) | json: {path, key, value} merged into a config file}, {mcp_server} = absolute path of mcp_server.py. Paths take ~ and ${VAR:-default}. headless_mcp = args `agents.py command … headless` adds so the run can use the blurt MCP server with no prompts (codex: the whole server via -c, since -c on an unregistered server breaks codex, plus approve mode and the BLURT_* env it forwards); {mcp_server_json} = that path as a JSON/TOML string. interactive.session (K5, sessions.py dispatch: an interactive agent in a tmux window or the app's pty) = {argv: args after the bin ({prompt} = the short hand-off prompt), prompt: 'arg' (default) | 'paste' (pasted into the window once it is up), hooks: 'claude' (--settings <job>.claude-settings.json with per-session hooks) | 'codex' (-c notify + -c hooks.*) | absent (status from the terminal only), mcp: args added when the user hasn't installed the blurt MCP server ({mcp_config_json} = a --mcp-config JSON) or 'headless_mcp' (reuse those args)}. interactive.session.sandboxed: true = the agent's sandbox can't write the repository's .git from a linked worktree (codex workspace-write), so its hand-off says to leave changes uncommitted and sessions.py finish commits them (the sandbox is never widened to .git). The codex session turns off its startup update check (-c check_for_update_on_startup=false): an update prompt at startup is input it must drain while the embedded terminal attaches. interactive.session.thread_name (codex) = how a session's thread gets the hand-off's title once its id is known (the hooks' session id): argv starts the CLI's JSON-RPC app server on stdio (same CODEX_HOME), then initialize → `method` {threadId, name}; best effort (sessions.py name-thread). interactive.desktop (claude) = the agent's desktop app (name: what the app calls it — Go to Claude) as a hand-off target (sessions.py dispatch --runner desktop): url ({folder_q} = the worktree / project folder, {prompt_q} = the hand-off prompt with the note inline, or the short prompt pointing at the note when the url would pass max_url), app = the app's bundle id per platform, open = what Go to Claude opens; continue = moving a running terminal session there (sessions.py continue-desktop): argv after the bin ({session} = the agent's session id), only from min_version and with the auth probe (the status args) saying logged in with a subscription (a non-empty subscription key, or one of auth_methods); the desktop app doesn't get a terminal session's --mcp-config, so without the blurt MCP installed (mcp.check) it is refused unless the user agreed to mark the items by hand (--without-mcp). interactive.waiting_patterns = regexes on the last 15 lines of the window meaning 'waiting for you' — only used while an agent's hooks aren't reporting (no hooks, hooks not yet live — claude's workspace-trust dialog fires none — or the user didn't trust them) — and for codex always, since its hooks don't cover a tool's questions. interactive.error_patterns = the same, meaning 'it can't work at all and stays open' (claude: not logged in): the session becomes an error with that line as its reason, until the agent's hooks report. Processing (v0.7): models = where the agent's models are listed ({list: [{id, name, cheap}]} | {cache: the CLI's own model cache, format, config: its config file for the current default}); model_args = how a model / an effort level is passed ({model}, {effort}); processing = the default for unattended organising runs ({model: id | 'cheapest' (the cache's or list's cheap model) | 'default' (the CLI's own setting), effort: level | 'default'}), overridden per agent by config record.agent_processing.<id>; usage = how a run reports the tokens it used (args added to the processing run + format | pattern with the number in group 1).
